name: Billy Cobham
hook: A jazz-fusion drummer whose slow 1974 track 'Heather' became one of the most-loved loops in 90s rap.

blurb.age7: A jazz drummer. A slow song he made in 1974 was later used in a famous rap song.
blurb.age13: Billy Cobham was born in Panama in 1944 and grew up in New York. He became famous as the drummer in the Mahavishnu Orchestra, a band that mixed jazz and loud rock, and then made his own albums. One of them, Crosswinds (1974), has a slow, drifting song called 'Heather'. Nineteen years later the Oakland producer A-Plus sped it up and turned it into '93 'til Infinity' for Souls of Mischief.
blurb.adult: Cobham is on the map as a sampled source rather than for his own lineage. He's the first of the sampled-artist hubs agreed in Q21, where each use of his records is a sample edge. His own place in jazz-rock fusion, as the drummer of the Mahavishnu Orchestra, belongs to a jazz lineage the map has deferred (BACKLOG, Deferred data).
